earlier_scan.source_named: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann 2005. Notes sur le systeme verbal du Sokoro (Rep. du Tchad); Yaranga & Yaranga 2019 grammar sketch (99pp). Not online.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives, resource listing for Sokoro [sok] (the Internet Archive snapshot 2015-09-19).
sources.note: 45 Sokoro items, almost all literacy materials (syllabaires 1999-2011, contes, proverbes, Dictionnaire visuel français-sokoro-arabe tchadien 2008). Facets show one 'Phonology / phonological description' item and contributors Martin, Gordon (2), Yaranga Abderahim (1), Yaranga Hamdan (1); page 2 and facet pages are not archived and live sil.org is could not be reached by automated download, so the phonology item (presumably Martin 1999) could not be opened.

sources.citation: Rendinger, Général de. 1949. Contribution à l'étude des langues nègres du Centre africain. Journal de la Société des Africanistes 19(2): 143-194.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'Langue Sokoro' section pp. 163-166 is grammar notes (pronouns, possessives, verb tenses) and vocabulary; only phonetic remark is 'confusion fréquente entre a et o'. The two 'accent tonique' remarks (pp. 147-148: a stressed vowel modifies neighbouring vowels; unstressed final vowel of a noun drops) are in the Kenga section, not Sokoro. Transcription accents mark vowel quality/length, not stress.

sources.citation: Afrika und Übersee open-access site, backlist page (Universität Hamburg).
sources.note: States 'Volumes 1-92 are not yet available in digital form'; hence Jungraithmayr 2005 (vol. 88: 175-186) is print-only (Harvard Widener Philol 14 per the earlier access table).

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 2020. [Notes on Saba]. Afrika und Übersee 93.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Saba (sister language) has two tone levels plus HL contour (section 2.3 'Les tons'). Sokoro mentioned only in fn. 2: Sokoro-Saba differences are considerable, intercomprehension about 50%, referring to Jungraithmayr 2005. Nothing on Sokoro stress.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann & Carsten Peust. 2019. Notes on Gàlì (Miltu), a moribund Chadic language (Republic of Chad). Folia Orientalia 56: 219-230.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology section is for Gàlì (three-level tone language). Sokoro appears only comparatively: tone-marked Sokoro lexemes from Jungraithmayr & Ibriszimow 1994 (gàgìr 'sheep', ɲéɗìyé 'to swallow', ùmbó 'water'), Sokoro verbal ablaut and future auxiliary gàrà citing Jungraithmayr 2005: 176. No statement on Sokoro stress.

sources.citation: Lovestrand, Joseph. 2012. Classification and description of the Chadic languages of the Guéra (East Chadic B). SIL Electronic Working Papers 2012-004, 1-59.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone for Sokoro. p. 44 gives a Sokoro consonant/vowel inventory 'Source: Martin 1999' (with tone-marked forms in the appendix wordlists, e.g. gə̀pə́n, kílmì), notes the mid central vowel is 'at best, a marginal phoneme (Martin 1999, Roberts 2009)'; lists Martin 1999 'Une esquisse phonologique de la langue Sokoro du Guéra' (SIL N'Djamena, manuscript), Chesley & Faris 1994, Fédry 1971, Jungraithmayr 2005b as Sokoro sources.
No phonology; reference list only (Benton 1912, Chesley & Faris 1994, Fédry 1971, Jungraithmayr 2005, Rendinger 1949).

sources.citation: Martin, Gordon. 1999. Une esquisse phonologique de la langue Sokoro du Guéra. N'Djamena: SIL. Manuscript.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only phonological description of Sokoro; source of Lovestrand's phoneme chart and of the tone-marked Sokoro forms; a phonology sketch is the place a tone/stress statement would be. Listed in the SIL archive facets for Sokoro ('phonological description', contributor Martin, Gordon).
